title: LFM2.5-VL-3B for Better and Faster Vision Capabilities for the Edge
gist: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-VL-3B, a 3.1B vision-language model pre-trained on ~34T tokens that deliberately answers directly instead of reasoning to keep on-device latency low. Its headline jumps are GUI/screen understanding (ScreenSpot-v2 Desktop 78.7 versus 6.0 for its own predecessor), grounding (RefCOCO 87.9 versus 57.1) and tool use (ToolSandbox 59.5 versus 26.4), while throughput of ~11K tokens/s at high concurrency implies nearly 1B output tokens per day on a single H100.

themes.theme: No-reasoning-by-design as an edge latency strategy

insights.claim: Liquid AI deliberately built LFM2.5-VL-3B to answer directly rather than reason, trading chain-of-thought accuracy for response latency in real-time and on-device applications.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Signals a market split between reasoning models sold on capability and non-reasoning models sold on latency and cost per token — different buyers, different economics.
insights.quote: It answers directly instead of reasoning, so responses stay fast in real-time and on-device apps.
insights.locator: LFM2.5-VL-3B is our most capable vision-language model

insights.claim: The four claimed improvements over prior releases are screen/UI understanding, grounding and object detection from natural language queries, multi-image reasoning, and function calling in both text-only and vision-text settings — a capability set aimed squarely at device agents rather than chat.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: The small-VLM roadmap has pivoted from captioning to phone/desktop agent primitives, which is where on-device assistants and RPA products will be built.

insights.claim: LFM2.5-VL-3B pairs a SigLIP2 400M NaFlex vision encoder with the same pre-trained backbone as the LFM2.5-2.6B text model and is pre-trained on about 34T tokens with 4x more vision data than previous releases.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: 34T tokens into a 3B model is an extreme token-to-parameter ratio, showing that small-model quality is now bought with training compute rather than parameters — sustaining data-center demand even as deployed models shrink.
insights.locator: How we trained our most capable vision-language model

insights.claim: To support non-Latin scripts Liquid AI doubled the vocabulary to 128K by extending the tokenizer in place rather than retraining from scratch, avoiding a full pre-training run for multilingual coverage.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: In-place tokenizer extension is a cheap route to new-language markets; expect it to become standard practice for vendors localizing existing checkpoints.
insights.quote: we doubled the vocabulary to 128K by extending the tokenizer in place rather than retraining from scratch

insights.claim: Post-training runs in two stages — supervised fine-tuning with knowledge distillation from a larger teacher plus Antidoom training, followed by multi-reward reinforcement learning.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Distillation-from-a-larger-teacher remains the engine behind small-model gains, meaning frontier-scale training runs stay economically necessary even for edge products.

themes.theme: Benchmark deltas: where the generation gain actually landed

insights.claim: Screen understanding is the single largest jump: ScreenSpot-v2 Desktop went from 6.0 in LFM2-VL-3B to 78.7, Mobile from 7.6 to 81.2 and Web from 2.5 to 82.2 at the same 3.1B size.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: GUI grounding went from essentially non-functional to state-of-the-art in one generation at constant size, which removes the main technical blocker for on-device UI agents.

insights.claim: Grounding improved from RefCOCO-avg 57.1 to 87.9 and multi-image understanding from BLINK 50.2 to 61.5 and MuirBench 34.9 to 58.3, beating every listed competitor including Qwen3.5-4B and InternVL 3.5 4B on RefCOCO.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Grounding and multi-image are the fastest-moving axes in small VLMs right now, so any product spec written against last-generation grounding numbers is already obsolete.

insights.claim: The 3.1B model posts an average of 69.4 across the vision suite, tying the 4.7B InternVL 3.5 4B (69.4) and beating gemma-4-E4B-it at 8B (59.7) while trailing Qwen3.5-4B (70.1).
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Parameter count has decoupled from vision capability — an 8B Gemma losing to a 3.1B model means memory-constrained deployments no longer face a big quality penalty.

insights.claim: Tool use improved sharply in one generation, with ToolSandbox rising from 26.4 to 59.5 and BFCL V4 from 20.5 to 32.5, putting the model on par with Gemma-4-E2B and Qwen3.5-2B on tool use.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Reliable function calling at 3B is the precondition for local agents that call device APIs — a capability threshold worth tracking for on-device assistant products.

insights.claim: The model's weakest relative results are in multimodal instruction following and academic reasoning: MM-IFEval 60.6 trails gemma-4-E2B-it (65.6) and gemma-4-E4B-it (68.2), MMMU-Pro sits at 30.5 versus 36.0 for Qwen3.5-4B, and IFBench at 25.8 trails four competitors.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: The direct-answer, no-reasoning design shows its cost on instruction-following and academic reasoning; buyers with complex prompt-compliance requirements should not assume parity.

insights.claim: InternVL 3.5 2B and 4B do not support function calling at all, leaving N/A entries on ToolSandbox and BFCL V4 in the published comparison.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Function calling is not yet table stakes in small VLMs, so it remains a genuine differentiator when selecting a model for agentic deployment.
insights.quote: InternVL 3.5 models do not support function-calling.

insights.claim: Evaluation used vLLM 0.26.0 with each model's recommended generation parameters, non-reasoning mode everywhere, and models prompted to answer directly without reasoning — a setup that structurally favours a model designed not to reason.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Disclosed but self-serving harness choices; comparisons against reasoning-capable competitors would likely narrow if chain-of-thought were enabled.
insights.quote: Non-reasoning mode is used everywhere, and models are prompted to directly answer without reasoning.

themes.theme: Inference economics on device and on H100

insights.claim: LFM2.5-VL-3B decodes 228 tokens/s on an M5 Max, 116 tokens/s on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 and 20 tokens/s on a Galaxy S26 Ultra while fitting in about 3 GB of memory, making full phone-side operation viable.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: A 3 GB memory footprint with usable phone throughput puts capable vision models inside current flagship handset budgets, pulling multimodal inference off cloud APIs.

insights.claim: At high concurrency the model reaches about 11K output tokens per second — roughly 2x the larger 4B-class models and ahead of even smaller 2B-class models — which Liquid AI translates into nearly 1B output tokens per day on a single H100.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Roughly a billion output tokens a day per H100 collapses the unit cost of high-volume vision workloads and undercuts per-token pricing from hosted multimodal APIs.
insights.quote: which adds up to nearly 1B output tokens per day on a single H100
insights.locator: LFM2.5-VL-3B is also the fastest on output throughput

insights.claim: Beating smaller 2B-class models on output throughput shows that architecture and serving efficiency, not parameter count, now determine tokens-per-second at high concurrency.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Cost-per-token modelling based on parameter count is unreliable; measured throughput at target concurrency is the only defensible input.

insights.claim: The model shipped with day-one support across llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang and ONNX, plus a browser WebGPU demo and transformers>=5.0.0 compatibility.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: Day-one runtime coverage is becoming the real distribution moat for open-weight releases — a model absent from llama.cpp and MLX at launch loses the edge developer audience.
insights.quote: LFM2.5-VL-3B ships with day-one support across the inference ecosystem, including llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX.
insights.locator: Inference speed on CPU and GPU

insights.claim: Liquid AI positions the model explicitly for high-volume on-device workloads rather than general assistant use, pairing that positioning with fine-tuning tutorials for task adaptation.
insights.speaker: Samuel Stevens
insights.so_what: The go-to-market is volume-based edge inference plus customization, competing on cost-per-task rather than benchmark leadership.
insights.quote: Reach for LFM2.5-VL-3B when you need on-device intelligence for high-volume workloads.
